pr_title: Adds --web flag to open codespace in vscode web
pr_body:
Fixes #4985

- Adds `--web` flag to open the codespace in vscode web. 
- updates `codespaces/api/api.go` `Codespace` type to include `WebUrl`
pr_comments:
> I added a couple of questions/suggestions based on other implementations of opening a resource on the browser when using the gh cli

Thanks for the review, @luanzeba. I've implemented the suggestions. I appreciate you catching the inconsistencies with other features.

issue_context.title: Create functionality to allow this command `gh cs open` to open the codespace in the browser.
issue_context.body:
It would be consistent with codespaces and the github CLI at large to **add a command to the `gh cs` that allows the end user to open the codespace environment in the browser, such as `open` ==> `gh cs open`**.

It would be just like `gh cs code` where it shows a dropdown of the choices of codespaces, and then instead of opening vs-code it would open up the OS's default browser which, if it's authenticated with github.com will proceed to the primary value proposition of Code Spaces: allow the end-users to easily embark on a cloud development experience without the hassle of clicking around github.com, in the comfort of their terminal.
comments:
Thanks for the suggestion!

We already have the `gh cs code` command to open VS Code app on your computer. I understand that you are proposing to open the VS Code environment in one's web browser, correct? Would this feature then better be expressed as a flag for the existing `code` command, e.g. `gh cs code --web`?

Yeah . . . `gh codespace code` or `gh codespace code --web` captures it. 

As an alternative. . . I went back and took a screenshot of the language when clicking on a codespace in the browser and it seems they use the verbiage `open in vs-code`, which kind of implies that what's happening in this screenshot is that we're `opening` the codespaces in the browser. So . . . one idea to consider is to remove `gh cs code` entirely and have `gh cs open` and `gh cs open --web`.

Whatever your team chooses I am stoked and flattered that you actually replied to my suggestion!! Thanks!

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/689723/148631342-09fd2294-78c8-456c-a09c-5a85db2e052f.png)

If someone wants to add a `gh cs code --web` flag with the described behavior, be our guest please! 👍 

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8198cce59b47eafc5bf20e6565e0d9497e534810/pkg/cmd/codespace/code.go#L33-L34
I would like to attempt to add this feature. Can I be assigned to this issue?
Hey @isenkasa are you still working on this? I'd like to take a stab at it if you're not

review_comments: This seems fine to me. I wonder how much usage this will get and whether `gh codespace web` might be warranted but we can always introduce that later.

I just realized that we are not respecting the `useInsiders` flag in case someone provides both that + the new `web` option. TIL that [VS Code for Web has an insiders build](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/vscode-web#_relationship-to-vs-code-desktop) at https://insiders.vscode.dev/

Although it doesn't look like that works for Codespaces when I tried it out. We should probably add a validation that checks only one of those flags is present otherwise provide an error to the user right above this.

There is an optional query param `vscodeChannel` that you can use to select the between `insiders` and `stable` - e.g. `https://<name>.github.dev/?vscodeChannel=insiders` - in order to handle the `--insiders` flag. I think you'd be able to  do something like `codespace.WebUrl + "?vscodeChannel=insiders"` below.
